questions.a: PHP (Hypertext Preprocessor) is a widely-used open-source server-side scripting language designed for web development. It can be embedded into HTML and runs on the server, generating dynamic page content. PHP is loosely typed, interpreted, and supports object-oriented programming.

questions.q: How do you declare variables in PHP?
questions.a: Variables in PHP start with a $ sign followed by the name. They are loosely typed â€” no type declaration is required. Example: $name = "John";. PHP 7+ supports typed properties in classes and PHP 8+ adds union types.

questions.q: What is the difference between echo and print?
questions.a: echo can output multiple strings separated by commas and is slightly faster. print returns 1 so it can be used in expressions. Both are language constructs (not functions), so parentheses are optional.
== (loose equality) coerces types before comparing, e.g. "5" == 5 is true. === (strict equality) checks both value and type, so "5" === 5 is false. Always prefer === for predictable comparisons.

questions.q: Explain PHP 8 attributes and their use.
questions.a: PHP 8.0+ attributes (annotations) add structured metadata to classes, methods, properties, etc. They use the #[Attribute] syntax. Attributes are read via reflection ($ref->getAttributes()). Laravel uses them for route definitions, event listeners, and model casting. Example: #[Route('get', '/dashboard')].
Fibers (PHP 8.1+) are lightweight coroutines for cooperative multitasking. A fiber can be suspended (Fiber::suspend()) and resumed ($fiber->resume()) from the main execution context.

PHP 8.4 introduced property hooks, allowing custom get/set logic for properties. Syntax: public string $name { get => ...; set => ...; }. Also asymmetric visibility (public private(set) string $email).

questions.q: Explain the SOLID principles in depth.
questions.a:
Single Responsibility: each class has one reason to change.
Open/Closed: open for extension, closed for modification.
Liskov Substitution: subtypes must be substitutable.
Interface Segregation: many specific interfaces > one general.
Dependency Inversion: depend on abstractions, not concretions.

questions.q: What are magic methods and their advanced use cases?
Compare Repository vs Active Record patterns.
questions.a:
Active Record (Eloquent): model handles data + persistence. Simple, rapid CRUD.
Repository: abstracts data access behind interface. Swap implementations, unit test with mocks. Use for complex domain logic, CQRS, hexagonal architecture.
